items.title: Louis Cottrell, Jr. Interview, 1961-08-25
items.q: And speaking of Simeon, T.O. used to tell me all the time when I was taking lessons from him, he always rated Simeon as his best scholar.

ctx.x: player in New York and also studied with T.O. Yeah. And up in Chicago, he says the same thing. He was so young he wasn't allowed to go around the dance halls. Well that's right. So you never really heard him play much. He can't remember much whether he used Albert or Bing's system, aren't he? Well I knew he used Albert. I can readily remember that. Well I think he knew that much but I mean he couldn't remember much about his instrument or how he played or sounded because he just took lessons and that was about all.

And speaking of Simeon, T.O. used to tell me all the time when I was taking lessons from him, he always rated Simeon as his best scholar. He did, huh? He did. He said for one reason, Simeon had that initiative and that determination to really learn and he said that's the only scholar that he ever had that he didn't have to send back the second time on the lesson. Yeah. Yeah. He said Simeon was just, just that way. And he said each time he came he was ready. There's no saying,
well come back, you don't know it that well this time. Uh-huh. That's about, what year now did you study with him? Let's see, you were born 1911.
